topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-14 15:00 UTC / Duration 46m / Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Karen (Spectra Head of SecOps), Diego (Spectra Platform Eng), Priya (Spectra Compliance)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have 45, 46 minutes on the calendar. quick round of intros?
[00:08] Karen: Karen O'Neill, head of SecOps at Spectra, happy to kick off, we're looking at inference providers for some customer-facing features.
[00:14] Diego: Diego Alvarez, platform eng, I'll be doing the integration work.
[00:18] Priya: Priya Shah, compliance manager, I'll be the point for questionnaires and controls.
[00:23] Maya: Great, Maya Patel, AE at Redwood, Jordan our SE is here to help on the technical side, and Ravi from CS to align on pilots.
[00:30] Jordan: hi everyone, yeah happy to dive into architecture and ops.
[00:35] Maya: Quick agenda, walk through security posture, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, SSO/SSO—SAML questions, encryption/KMS, retention, and next steps. Sound good?
[00:45] Karen: Yep, let's go. main ask from our execs: we need SOC 2 and ISO attestations and clear notes on where customer data resides. Also we have strict retention limits and egress controls.
[00:56] Maya: Totally understood. We are SOC 2 Type II and we maintain ISO 27001—I'll share the attestation PDFs after the call. Hosted customers get data logically segregated, we have regional controls for residency. For the most strict setups we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.
[01:15] Priya: When you say "logically segregated" can you be concrete? our auditors push back on multi-tenant wording.
[01:22] Jordan: sure, for hosted we do tenant isolation at the application layer plus encryption at rest per-tenant keys, access controls and audit logging. For dedicated, you get reserved GPU pools and network isolation, and for private you can have a customer-managed VPC or on-prem. I should say the wording in our SOC docs clarifies logical separation, happy to point to the exact control language.
[01:45] Diego: How about SSO, we run Okta. we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning.
[01:52] Maya: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We also support SAML-based Just-in-Time provisioning for some roles. We'll share the Okta setup doc. There may be minor differences if you go Private vs Hosted (e.g. metadata exchange endpoints), but the flows are the same.
[02:10] Priya: RBAC—how granular can we be? We want to ensure least privilege: product teams can call inference but only a small set of ops can manage keys and configs.
[02:18] Jordan: Our Console supports role-based permissions that map to things like model deploy, route config, billing, and admin. You can integrate with Okta groups via SCIM and have those translated into roles. For Dedicated we can set up more restrictive network-level admin roles.
[02:35] Karen: Audit logs are big for us. do you store detailed per-request logs and how long do they retain? Also, are logs tamper-evident?
[02:44] Maya: We store audit trails for admin actions and request metadata for a configurable period. Default retention is 90 days for hosted analytics, but we offer extended retention as an add-on. For tamper evidence, logs are write-once within our system and we provide export hooks to your SIEM via secure forwarder or S3 with signed URLs. For Private you can push logs directly to your Splunk/Datadog.
[03:05] Priya: And do those logs contain customer prompt content? that's sensitive.
[03:10] Jordan: Good question—by default request transcripts (prompt/content) are not stored in our analytics store for hosted; we store metadata and token counts. You can opt-in to store full transcripts for debugging in a controlled way, but that requires additional controls and consent. For workloads requiring no persistence of prompts, we can enable ephemeral inference paths where prompt content isn't persisted beyond the processing window.
[03:33] Diego: Ok that's helpful. next: encryption and KMS. we require customer-managed keys for production PII processing. do you support BYOK and HSM integrations?
[03:41] Maya: Yes, we support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) via standard KMS integrations, including AWS KMS and GCP Cloud KMS. For Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM so that keys are customer-controlled. For Hosted, we offer customer-managed CMKs with encryption envelopes and key rotation policies.
[04:00] Priya: Any certifications around the KMS/HSM side?
[04:03] Jordan: We integrate with regular cloud KMS options which are FIPS-compliant, and for on-prem HSMs we have vetted partners. We can include details in the security questionnaire response.
[04:16] Karen: Data residency—some of our EU customers need data to stay in EU region. can you pin regions for hosted?
[04:22] Maya: Yes, you can select region in hosted, we have EU regions. If you need strong physical isolation, Dedicated or Private in an EU region is recommended. We can provide data flow diagrams for the architecture.
[04:34] Diego: Latency vs cost: our product needs sub-200ms for short completions. hosted looks cheaper but worried about tail latency. What are typical SLOs?
[04:43] Jordan: For small prompt sizes and local region routing we commonly see median latencies under 120ms for short inference, but tail latency can vary depending on load. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity with much tighter SLOs and predictable p99s. There are tradeoffs with cost — Dedicated has a committed cost but lower per-token unit price for heavy steady traffic.
[05:06] Maya: Also we do prefix caching and batching tunables to reduce cost without impacting latency for many use cases. We'll include a sample configuration for your traffic profile.
[05:16] Priya: About audits—do you allow customer audits or provide SOC attestations only?
[05:21] Maya: We provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 reports. For more detailed audits—on Dedicated or Private, we can provide more access and scopes for customer audits; for hosted we facilitate auditor access with data minimization and controlled scopes. We'll outline the process in the security pack.
[05:36] Karen: Our legal team will want the incident response plan and breach notification SLA.
[05:40] Ravi: We have an incident response playbook and 72-hour notification SLA for customer-impacting incidents, with a published status page and a private incident channel for enterprise customers. We'll include the IR summary in the packet.
[05:55] Diego: Question on model artifacts—where do you store model weights? Can we pin to an approved model and have checksum validation?
[06:03] Jordan: Model weights are stored in our artifact storage in encrypted blobs. For Dedicated/Private you can pin a specific model version and we provide checksums and attestations. For hosted we maintain model provenance and versions; we can export checksums to you for validation.
[06:20] Priya: We usually have a vendor security questionnaire. timeline wise we need answers in two weeks if possible.
[06:27] Maya: Sounds doable. We'll commit to returning the completed questionnaire and SOC/ISO PDFs by June 16th. Jordan will prepare a Dedicated estimate and Ravi will set follow-up.
[06:36] Karen: On egress controls—if we decide to terminate, can we export logs and data? what's the process and retention for egress?
[06:44] Jordan: Yes, customers can request full export of retained data via S3 export or encrypted bundle. We also have a deletion certification once data is removed. Retention defaults and export windows will be noted in the contract.
[06:58] Diego: If we go Private on-prem, are there offline install packages?
[07:02] Maya: Yes, we have an on-prem package and an air-gapped installer for highly regulated customers. Implementation timelines are longer but doable. We'll put notes in the follow-up doc.
[07:12] Priya: Any third-party penetration testing?
[07:15] Jordan: We run annual pen tests and vulnerability scans; summary reports are available under an NDA.
[07:22] Karen: Let's talk risk appetite: we have a requirement that no full PII should be stored in third-party logs. you mentioned ephemeral paths—can we get contractual language for that?
[07:31] Maya: Yes, for the pilot we can enable ephemeral mode and include language around no-persistence of prompts. We'll include a proposed addendum for the contract.
[07:42] Diego: Implementation question: what does the integration look like? is there an SDK and REST API, or do we do direct gRPC?
[07:49] Jordan: REST and SDKs (Python/Node) are common, and we also support gRPC for lower-latency flows. We'll share sample code and a small quickstart repo.
[08:01] Priya: About RBAC again—need separation for dev/test vs prod, can you enforce network egress controls so dev doesn't access prod keys?
[08:09] Jordan: Yes, environment segmentation is supported. Keys can be scoped per-environment and network rules can restrict egress. For Dedicated we can further restrict inter-environment communication.
[08:21] Karen: Are there legal templates around data processing agreements and subprocessor lists? our legal will want that.
[08:27] Maya: We have a DPA and subprocessor list; we'll include the latest versions.
[08:33] Diego: What about pricing for extended retention and audit exports?
[08:36] Maya: We'll include an options matrix—retention tiers, export frequency, and associated costs in the pricing pack.
[08:44] Priya: For compliance we need log integrity for 1 year. Is that supported without huge cost?
[08:50] Jordan: Yes, extended retention add-on supports 1-year logs; cost depends on volume but we can provide a ballpark estimate.
[08:59] Maya: Quick recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, security questionnaire answers, Okta SAML/SCIM setup doc, Dedicated capacity estimate, retention/pricing matrix, IR summary, and notes on BYOK/HSM. Ravi will coordinate follow-up.
[09:14] Karen: perfect. timeline for next call? we prefer early next week.
[09:18] Ravi: I'll send a Doodle and propose Tuesday 10am PST.
[09:23] Diego: good. thanks everyone.
[09:26] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors in proper nouns (e.g., "Redwood Dedicaed" vs "Dedicated"), filler words and overlaps. References to docs: Security pack (link to be provided), Okta SAML setup doc, Dedicated sizing spreadsheet.

End of meeting.
